subject: science
prompt:
# Before We Solve It

Proto's useful molecules are floating loose in the ocean. They work well together - when they happen to be together. Currents keep pulling them apart.

> **Suppose you wrap them in a boundary. What is the catch?**

Pick the problem you think a boundary creates. We will come back to your answer.

options.text: There is no catch. A boundary solves the problem completely.
options.feedback: Hold that thought. By the end of the lesson there is a whole new problem waiting.

options.text: A boundary that keeps things in also keeps things out.
A boundary would make the molecules stop reacting with each other.
options.feedback: Bringing them closer together does the opposite - reactions get easier, not harder.

options.text: The molecules would be too heavy to float once wrapped up.
options.feedback: Weight is not the difficulty here. Think about what has to cross the boundary.
